pr_title: Work around the absence of SpeculationReasonEncoding in OpenJDK11
pr_body:
Fixes #2933

Note that this PR fixes only the specific issue discussed in #2933, which is necessary to create a Mandrel build based on graalvm's master.  Even after merging this PR parts of GraalVM will fail to build using OpenJDK 11, for instance `mx --primary-suite-path substratevm --components='Native Image' build` will fail.
pr_comments:
> What I had in mind was to access `UnencodedSpeculationReason` fields `context` and `groupId` reflectively from the code in `com.oracle.svm.graal.isolated`, and to call the `SpeculationReasonEncodingClone` methods directly. This has the advantage that the native image build can reliably turn the reflective accesses into direct field accesses.

I followed this approach which made things a bit simpler. Thanks. Does the rest (other than error checking and caching) look OK?
Hi @peter-hofer could you please let me know if this is moving in the right direction?
Converting to draft till I get the test working.
I'll run our tests on the current state and let you know.

Looks good overall, but there is another problem: for JDK 8, we have a class `GraalServices.EncodedSpeculationReason` which the current code tries to cast to `jdk.vm.ci.meta.EncodedSpeculationReason` and fails.
@dougxc , how come we need that extra class on JDK 8 rather than using `jdk.vm.ci.meta.EncodedSpeculationReason` or `UnencodedSpeculationReason` like on JDK 11?
I cannot recall the reasons. I think using `jdk.vm.ci.meta.EncodedSpeculationReason` should work.

Thank you @olpaw and @dougxc

I made `GraalServices.createSpeculationReason()` use  `jdk.vm.ci.meta.EncodedSpeculationReason` and removed `GraalServices.EncodedSpeculationReason`.
I changed the compliance level of the junit tests I added to "8+" so that we can use them for both JDK 8 and 11.
I also augmented the native junit test to test `GraalServices.createSpeculationReason()` as well.

issue_context.title: "cannot find symbol SpeculationReasonEncoding" when building with vanilla OpenJDK
issue_context.body:
**Describe the issue**
As discussed in https://github.com/graalvm/mandrel/issues/146 after @2d5eee0 GraalVM no longer builds with vanilla OpenJDK.

> It looks like oracle@2d5eee0 depends on https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8220623 which got backported to labsJDK11 in graalvm/labs-openjdk-11@fbbdf5f

Unfortunately https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8220623 is rather big and includes many changes that are not all related to the issue at hand. I tried creating a minimal backport/patch for jdk11u by pulling in only the needed changes but I ended up pulling more and more dependencies (especially after entering the C++ code).  The main issue seems to be the way that failed speculations are gathered after https://bugs.openjdk.java.net/browse/JDK-8220623. I also tried pulling in only the necessary changes without changing the way that failed speculations are gathered, but then the `SpeculationReasonEncoding` is not actually used making this kind of patch kind of pointless.

So I am openning this issue to ask for directions on how to approach this and discuss possible alternatives.

Thanks! 

**Steps to reproduce the issue**
```
export JAVA_HOME=/tmp/openjdk11ea
curl -sL https://api.adoptopenjdk.net/v3/binary/latest/11/ea/linux/x64/jdk/hotspot/normal/openjdk -o jdk.tar.gz
curl -sL https://api.adoptopenjdk.net/v3/binary/latest/11/ea/linux/x64/staticlibs/hotspot/normal/openjdk -o jdk-static-libs.tar.gz
mkdir -p ${JAVA_HOME}
tar xf jdk.tar.gz -C ${JAVA_HOME} --strip-components=1
tar xf jdk-static-libs.tar.gz -C ${JAVA_HOME} --strip-components=1
git clone git@github.com:oracle/graal.git --depth 1
cd graal
mx --primary-suite-path substratevm build --projects=com.oracle.svm.graal
```

**Describe GraalVM and your environment:**
 - GraalVM version: **master branch (60faf95321609669bcf0a01e0e134c3b7906e435)**
 - JDK major version: **11**
 - OS: **Linux Fedora 32**
 - Architecture: **AMD64**

**More details**
```
$ mx --primary-suite-path substratevm build --projects=com.oracle.svm.graal         
Compiling com.oracle.svm.graal with javac-daemon(JDK 11)... [dependencies were added, removed or re-ordered]
/home/zakkak/code/graal/substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.graal/src/com/oracle/svm/graal/isolated/IsolatedSpeculationReason.java:41: error: cannot find symbol
    public SpeculationLog.SpeculationReasonEncoding encode(Supplier<SpeculationLog.SpeculationReasonEncoding> encodingSupplier) {
                                                                                  ^
  symbol:   class SpeculationReasonEncoding
  location: interface SpeculationLog
/home/zakkak/code/graal/substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.graal/src/com/oracle/svm/graal/isolated/IsolatedSpeculationReason.java:41: error: cannot find symbol
    public SpeculationLog.SpeculationReasonEncoding encode(Supplier<SpeculationLog.SpeculationReasonEncoding> encodingSupplier) {
                         ^
  symbol:   class SpeculationReasonEncoding
  location: interface SpeculationLog
/home/zakkak/code/graal/substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.graal/src/com/oracle/svm/graal/isolated/IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding.java:40: error: cannot find symbol
final class IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding extends ByteArrayOutputStream implements SpeculationLog.SpeculationReasonEncoding {
                                                                                                     ^
  symbol:   class SpeculationReasonEncoding
  location: interface SpeculationLog
3 errors

Compiling com.oracle.svm.graal with javac-daemon(JDK 11) failed
1 build tasks failed
```
comments:
This is how @dougxc and I think this can be fixed:
1. Unimplement interface `SpeculationReasonEncoding` in `IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding` and create and implement a new interface that is identical.
1. `UnencodedSpeculationReason` is the class instantiated by `GraalServices` when `EncodedSpeculationReason` and `SpeculationReasonEncoding` are not available. Duplicate the code in `EncodedSpeculationReason` that does the encoding and change it so it does the same on an `UnencodedSpeculationReason` using reflection, using the new encoding interface created in step 1.
1. In `IsolatedSpeculationLog.maySpeculate` and `.speculate`, do an `instanceof` check on the argument. If it is an `UnencodedSpeculationReason`, use the duplicated code to get a byte array to pass over the isolate boundary. If it is any other class, use a `java.lang.Proxy` to implement `SpeculationReasonEncoding` that delegates to `IsolatedSpeculationReasonEncoding` and use reflection to invoke the `encode` method. Cache the proxy and reflection accessors in static variables.
Thanks a lot @peter-hofer and @dougxc! I'll give it a go and come back :)

Hello @peter-hofer, please find a draft PR [here](https://github.com/oracle/graal/pull/2945) implementing the above suggestions. I am not sure how to test these specific parts though, so please let me know how to test them if they are not covered by the standard `mx gate`.

review_comments: This comment should also explain why copying is necessary so that no one is tempted to "uncopy" it.
This and `getEntryPoint` are `final` in vanilla openjdk11

If I understand the review conversation, these reflective accesses will be converted to non-reflective accesses during image building. A comment should be added somewhere here explaining that. Does the added unit test check that this happens?

> Does the added unit test check that this happens?

Not at its current state. It cannot be compiled with native-image due to the invocation handler that is required to create the supplier that we pass to labsJDK's internal `encode`.
Would adding another test that only uses graalvm's implementations and running it with `native-unittest` be enough?
If that tests the condition stated in the (to be added) comment, then yes.

According to https://www.graalvm.org/reference-manual/native-image/Reflection/ 

>  If the target elements can be resolved, the calls are removed and instead the target elements are embedded in the code. If the target elements cannot be resolved, e.g., a class is not on the classpath or it does not declare a field/method/constructor, then the calls are replaced with a snippet that throws the appropriate exception at run time.

So to my understanding just compiling and running an image that covers the corresponding code segments should be enough.

Is there any better way to achieve this?
Indeed, if the members cannot be resolved directly and are not registered by other means, usually a configuration file, using them will fail.

Feedback from internal review: 

> Instead of reflection, it is better to use a method handle returned by `MethodHandles.lookup().unreflectGetter` and stored in a static final field. The method handle is then really intrinsified to a direct field access.

Looks like the accesses cannot be intrinsified from within the code, but what if you store the accessors in a `static final` field? It should be possible to move the class detection logic to a `static` initializer for that.

Tried that as well (see https://github.com/zakkak/mandrel/commit/8a6a7967324b1ab2ee73a5474b9245386b6e6dd3), but it still gives
```
Error: com.oracle.graal.pointsto.constraints.UnsupportedFeatureException: Invoke with MethodHandle argument could not be reduced to at most a single call or single field access. The method handle must be a compile time constant, e.g., be loaded from a `static final` field. Method that contains the method handle invocation: java.lang.invoke.LambdaForm$MH/658839328.invoke_MT(Object, Object, Object)
```
at
https://github.com/zakkak/mandrel/commit/8a6a7967324b1ab2ee73a5474b9245386b6e6dd3#diff-603f78c0054580a456da1e1f763e13bd03cd60958a2f5358fb25509c268d57f6R104

I finally got around to look into this today, sorry for the delay. The issue is that calling the getter on the interface type (rather than a concrete subclass which is guaranteed to have the accessed fields) introduces a type-check, which makes the method handle logic too complex to inline.
I'll merge the reflection variant.

Thank you @peter-hofer!
Could you please outline the process you used to figure this out (if possible with tools available to the community)?

I tried creating bgv files from building the native `native-image` but I couldn't find the graph for `encodeAsByteArray`.

From debugging the code that creates the error in `IntrinsifyMethodHandlesInvocationPlugin`, I could gather that the method handle graph contains an `If` node where it isn't supported. I then used the command line `mx native-unittest IsolatedSpeculationLog --build-args -H:Dump=:1 -H:MethodFilter=encodeAsByteArray` to get a bgv file with the method handle graph that cannot be inlined and saw that it has a type check.
I then consulted with @christianwimmer who told me to look at the parameter node's type. That turned out to be `SpeculationReason`, which is an interface that of course doesn't have the accessed field(s), so the type check is necessary. Since we use `Class.forName` and so cannot define a statically typed variable of the subclass with the fields, we cannot proceed.
That helps a lot, thank you for the information @peter-hofer
